about.intro: Goloka is a free, ad-free index of ISKCON content on YouTube — lectures, kirtans, festivals, and documentaries from dozens of temples and teachers, gathered in one calm place instead of scattered across the platform.
about.indexBody: Goloka stores no video files. Every listing is metadata — a title, a thumbnail, a category — and every video plays through YouTube's own standard embedded player. Watching here is the same as watching on YouTube directly; Goloka just makes it easier to find.
about.belongsTitle: All content belongs to its creators
about.belongsBody: Every video links back to its source channel. Goloka doesn't re-host, re-edit, or monetize anyone's content — it's simply a directory pointing to work that already belongs to the temples and speakers who made it.
about.privacyBody1: Signed out, Goloka keeps nothing about you at all. "Continue Watching" lives only in your own browser and is never sent anywhere — clearing your browser data clears it completely. Chanting while signed out is the same: your rounds stay on your device alone and reset each day, kept nowhere else.
about.privacyBody2: Signing in is optional, and it exists so your practice can follow you: your favourites and watch-later list, your japa record by day, month and year, and — new in July 2026 — your watch history, so "Continue Watching" carries from your phone to your laptop. That is everything an account holds. It is yours alone: never shared, never compared with anyone, never sold, and never used to build an advertising profile. Delete your account and everything it held is deleted with it.
about.independentBody: Goloka is an independent, non-commercial project — not an official ISKCON website, and not affiliated with any single temple. It runs entirely on free-tier infrastructure, with no ads and nothing for sale.
about.helpBody: Know a channel that belongs here, or spot something miscategorized? <sendNote>Send a note</sendNote> — every suggestion is read.

books.essentialsSubtitle: From the official BBT store only — Goloka links, never sells.
books.disclaimer: All books and goods are published and sold by the Bhaktivedanta Book Trust and official ISKCON outlets. Goloka is an index — it hosts nothing and earns nothing from these links.

browse.byThemeBlurb: Categories say what a video is. These say what it is about — collections gathered across every channel.

leaders.intro: ISKCON teachers and speakers whose talks, kirtans and classes are indexed on Goloka.

start.welcomeP1: You don't need to believe anything to be here. You don't need to know a word of Sanskrit, or have read a single page of scripture, or have ever set foot inside a temple. None of that was ever the door - you're already standing inside it.
start.welcomeP2: Think of this simply as an invitation: to sit for a few quiet minutes and meet someone named Kṛṣṇa, through the eyes of people who love him very much. There is nothing to sign, nothing to join, no test waiting at the end. Watch if you'd like. Pause whenever you'd like. Come back whenever you'd like - or don't, and know you were welcome all the same.
start.welcomeP3: Below are ten small questions, each answered gently by a short video, one leading softly to the next. You don't have to take them in order, and you don't have to take them all. If all you ever watch is the first one, you will still have been received here exactly as you are. Let's begin gently.
start.videoUnavailable: This video isn't available right now - check back soon.
start.outroBody: The mahā-mantra itself is only a breath away - visit <chant>the chant</chant> and say the holy names for yourself. Or go deeper into the <books>Sacred Library</books>, where the Bhagavad-gītā waits as a natural next read. Or find a <temples>temple</temples> near you, and see one of these evenings with your own eyes.
start.outroClose: And whenever you're ready - simply begin.

install.intro: Goloka can live on your home screen like any other app — its own icon, full screen, no address bar. It is the same Goloka, only closer to hand.
install.free: There is nothing to download from an app store, no account is needed, and it takes about ten seconds.
install.alreadyInstalled: Goloka is already installed on this device — you are using it right now.

android.title: Add Goloka to your home screen
android.step2: Tap the three-dot menu at the top right.
android.step3: Tap "Add to Home screen" — some versions of Chrome say "Install app" instead.
android.step4: Tap "Install" to confirm. The gold lotus appears alongside your other apps.
android.note: If a gold install button appeared higher up this page, it does all of this in one tap.

ios.title: Add Goloka to your home screen
ios.step1: Open Goloka in Safari. On an iPhone or iPad this works only in Safari — not Chrome, not Firefox.
ios.step2: Tap the Share icon at the bottom of the screen: a square with an arrow pointing up out of it.
ios.step3: Scroll down the list of options and tap "Add to Home Screen".
ios.step5: The gold lotus is now on your home screen. Open Goloka from there rather than from Safari.
ios.note: Opening it from the home screen is what gives you the full screen — and on iPhone it is also the only way festival reminders can reach you.

desktop.title: Install Goloka as a desktop app
desktop.step1: Open Goloka in Chrome or Edge.
desktop.step2: Look in the address bar for the install icon — a small screen with an arrow pointing down into it — and click it.
desktop.step3: Click "Install". Goloka opens in its own window from then on.
desktop.note: Safari and Firefox on the desktop do not offer this. Bookmarking the site works just as well there.

install.whatYouGetBody: Goloka opens full screen with no address bar, starts from your home screen, and keeps its place in whatever you were watching. Everything else is exactly the same site — videos still play through YouTube's own player, and no video is ever downloaded to your device.
install.storageNote: Installing stores nothing extra about you. It does not create an account and it does not switch on notifications; both of those stay opt-in, exactly where you left them.
